title: Plural Nouns: One and Many
summary: In this lesson, you will learn how to talk about more than one thing. We will look at regular and irregular plural nouns.

sections.p: Most English words are regular. When you have two or more of something, you just add an 's' to the end of the word. For example, one cat becomes two cats. This is the easiest way to make a word plural, and you will use it every day when you speak and write in English.

ex.en: I have one cat and two dogs.
Please buy three apples at the store.
My books are on the table.

sections.p: Some words end with special sounds like ch, sh, s, or x. You cannot just add an 's' to these words. Instead, you must add '-es' to the end so it is easy to say. For example, one box becomes two boxes, and one bus becomes two buses.

ex.en: I wash the dishes every evening.
There are two buses on the street.
She has three boxes of shoes.

sections.p: Some common English words do not follow the rules. They change their spelling completely when they become plural! For example, one child becomes two children, and one man becomes two men. You need to memorize these special words because people use them all the time.

ex.en: The children are playing in the park.
I see two men near the door.

tip: Make a flashcard for irregular words like child and children. Practice saying them out loud every day!

quiz.en: I have two ___ in my bag.
The ___ are waiting for the bus.
She bought four ___ at the market.
My ___ hurt after walking all day.
